title: Hydrogen ion-slice stacking of 32 single-crystal silicon tiers
idea: Implant H+ into a pre-doped donor Si wafer, oxide-bond it onto the growing stack at <=350 C, cleave at the hydrogen plane, CMP, pattern only the lateral access transistors, and repeat ~32 times, reusing each donor ~10x; all capacitors are then formed by one vertical etch through every tier.
why: Removes the 3D-DRAM lateral-transistor blocker (fact 2) by giving every tier bulk-grade mobility and a tight leakage tail (fact 3), without the strain limit of Si/SiGe epi stacks; targets 26+ crystalline tiers and ~3-4x bits per wafer vs planar 1z.

title: Boron nitride monolayers shrink inter-tier spacers to three nanometers
idea: Replace the 20-30 nm SiO2 spacer between 3D-DRAM tiers with 2-3 layers of hexagonal BN (6 eV gap, pinhole-free van der Waals insulator) grown on a sacrificial template and transferred or directly grown by low-temperature plasma CVD, cutting tier pitch from ~60 nm to ~35 nm.
why: Hole-etch depth, not tier count, caps 3D DRAM (facts 1, 2); 1.7x more tiers in the same ~6 um stack reaches the 26-tier breakeven at a far lower etch aspect ratio.

title: Carbon wordlines: conformal nanographite replaces tungsten in replacement-gate cavities
idea: After the sacrificial nitride is pulled from each tier, fill the lateral wordline cavities with catalyst-free plasma-grown nanocrystalline graphite (C2H2, ~450 C) and intercalate it with FeCl3 to cut sheet resistance; no WF6, no fluorine attack on the gate oxide and no TiN barrier liner.
why: Removes tungsten (China ~80%) and the 3-5 nm liner that eats tier thickness; ~15% thinner tiers per stack height and a W-free 3D DRAM bill of materials.

title: Nitrogen: aluminum-nitride inter-tier heat spreaders hold retention in hot stacks
idea: Use sputtered/ALD polycrystalline AlN (30-100 W/mK vs 1.4 for SiO2) as every third inter-tier dielectric and as the bonding dielectric of memory-on-logic stacks, with AlN-filled dummy holes acting as vertical thermal pillars to the lid.
why: Leakage roughly doubles every ~10 C, so 3D DRAM over hot logic loses retention (fact 3); cutting stack temperature rise by 10-15 C halves refresh energy and lets DRAM sit directly on accelerators (fact 5).

title: Liquid-nitrogen-only 3D DRAM with tenfold smaller lateral capacitors
idea: Design a 3D DRAM exclusively for 77 K immersion pods (LN2 is cheap, abundant and US-made): subthreshold leakage falls >10^6x, so a lateral cell with a ~0.5 fF capacitor that fits inside a 25 nm tier, paired with very short local bitlines, retains data for seconds.
why: Dissolves the capacitor charge wall (fact 1) and the 3D capacitor blocker (fact 2); refresh approaches zero (fact 3) and tier pitch roughly halves, ~2x tiers per stack height, with cooling cost offset by lower wire resistance and no refresh.

title: Oxygen: porous-silicon oxidation carves many SOI tiers from one epi stack
idea: Grow an epi stack alternating p+ (~1e19) and lightly doped Si, open slits, anodize in HF so only the p+ layers become mesoporous, then oxidize them at ~850 C into buried oxide (FIPOS); the lightly doped layers remain single-crystal device tiers.
why: Crystalline multi-tier SOI with no germanium (no SiGe mismatch limit on tier count) and no bonding cycles; attacks the lateral-transistor blocker (fact 2) at epi-reactor cost.

title: Sodium-ion electret back-gates set each tier's threshold without wiring
idea: Implant a controlled Na+ dose into the buried oxide beneath each tier of p-channel lateral access transistors, drift it to the BOX top in a one-time field anneal, then seal it with SiN; the frozen charge acts as a permanent back-gate bias raising |Vt| by ~0.3 V.
why: Cuts the access-transistor leakage tail (fact 3) ~10x, stretching refresh intervals, with no negative wordline pump or per-tier back-gate contacts that would add staircase and periphery area (fact 7).

title: Magnesium sacrificial layers leave air-gap bitlines between 3D tiers
idea: Deposit thin Mg films flanking each horizontal bitline in the tier stack; after sealing, dilute acetic acid fed through slits dissolves the Mg (orders of magnitude faster than Si, SiO2 or TiN), leaving each bitline suspended in a low-k air gap.
why: Bitline capacitance falls ~40%, so the Cs/Cb ratio improves and the cell capacitor can shrink ~40% at equal sense signal, easing the charge wall (fact 1) and bitline CV2 energy (fact 10).

title: Aluminum-doped zinc oxide shield planes stop vertical row-hammer coupling
idea: Insert a 5 nm ALD Al:ZnO conductive plane, grounded through the staircase, between each pair of 3D-DRAM tiers so an aggressor wordline in tier k couples into the shield instead of victim cells in tiers k+1 and k-1.
why: 3D stacking adds vertical hammer and crosstalk paths (fact 9); a grounded shield cuts inter-tier coupling ~90%, allowing tighter tier pitch without new hammer exposure, using only Al, Zn and O at 200 C.

title: Silicon seed-window lateral overgrowth grows each crystalline tier in place
idea: Over each finished tier, deposit oxide, open a sparse grid of seed windows to the crystalline tier below and grow Si by selective epitaxial lateral overgrowth until fronts merge, then CMP to 30 nm; merge seams are laid out under wordline-cut and dummy regions.
why: Single-crystal stacked tiers without bonding or germanium (fact 2); periphery is hybrid-bonded later so the epi thermal budget is tolerable, and the array layout is co-designed around seam locations.

title: Silicon carbide vertical 4F2 cells for near-refresh-free retention
idea: Build vertical-channel 4F2 cells in 4H-SiC (3.3 eV gap) on the 200 mm SiC wafer base scaled for EV power devices: implanted buried n+ bitlines, trench gate-all-around channels and a stacked capacitor on top, where intrinsic carrier density ~1e-9 cm^-3 suppresses junction and GIDL leakage by >1e8 vs Si.
why: Attacks the leakage tail (fact 3), aiming at minutes of retention so refresh power and bandwidth loss vanish, while tapping a US-anchored substrate and tool base outside the DRAM supply chain.

title: Phosphorus delta-doped epitaxial sheets serve as built-in buried bitlines
idea: In a monolithic Si epi tier stack, grow each horizontal bitline as an in-situ phosphorus-doped (>1e20) epitaxial sheet that the slit etch later segments into short local bitlines, so the bitline is a crystalline conductor formed during growth rather than metal pushed into 100:1 lateral cavities.
why: Removes the hardest metal fill of vertical-wordline 3D DRAM (fact 2) and its tungsten; the bitline self-aligns to its transistor tier, saving a critical mask per tier group.

title: Sulfur-vapor conversion of patterned molybdenum gives per-tier MoS2 channels
idea: In each BEOL tier, sputter 1-2 nm Mo pre-patterned into channel islands and convert it to MoS2 in sulfur vapor at ~450 C (no H2S); the 0.65 nm channel keeps electrostatics ideal in a 20 nm lateral transistor and its 1.8 eV gap limits off-current.
why: An ultrathin, low-leakage, indium-free lateral transistor solves the 3D blocker (fact 2) at BEOL thermal budget; ~15 nm tiers instead of ~40 nm double tiers per stack height.

title: Calcium fluoride and silicon epitaxial superlattice yields insulated crystalline tiers
idea: Exploit CaF2's 0.6% lattice match to Si to grow Si/CaF2 epitaxial superlattices by MBE or low-temperature CVD, so every Si layer is a single-crystal device tier and every CaF2 layer (12 eV gap) is a built-in insulator that can also be recessed selectively to open capacitor cavities.
why: One-pass growth of crystalline SOI-like tiers with no bonding and no germanium (fact 2), from abundant Ca and F; CaF2 doubles as isolation and sacrificial layer.

title: Titanium dioxide rutile on fluorine-tin-oxide electrodes for compact lateral capacitors
idea: Use conductive F-doped SnO2 (rutile structure, ALD at ~250 C) as the storage-node electrode so ALD TiO2 nucleates directly as rutile (k ~80-100) instead of anatase (k ~30), replacing Ru-templated stacks; 1% Al doping plus a thin Al2O3 interlayer hold leakage.
why: Delivers the k ~70+ the charge wall needs (fact 1), so lateral 3D-DRAM capacitors shrink to short cups inside a tier instead of 60-75:1 pillars, using only Sn, Ti, F and O.

title: Titanium nitride mirror plate pillar serves two cell strings per hole
idea: Lay out 3D DRAM so each vertical TiN plate-line pillar sits between two mirrored lateral cell strings whose capacitors both wrap that same pillar; one deep plate etch and fill serves twice the cells and anchors the alignment of both strings.
why: Halves the deep plate/capacitor holes per bit and recovers ~25% of array footprint in vertical-wordline 3D DRAM (fact 2), cutting critical etch and litho steps (fact 4).

title: Vanadium dioxide graded-threshold switches replace the tier staircase
idea: Run one shared vertical select pillar per block through all tiers with a VO2 insulator-metal-transition switch at each tier junction, its thickness graded so switching voltage steps ~0.15 V per tier; ramping this pillar against a counter-pillar opens exactly one tier using two contacts instead of 32.
why: The staircase and per-tier contacts grow in area and mask count with tiers (facts 2, 7); collapsing them into two pillars could save ~5-10% die area and many staircase litho/etch cycles.

title: Iron-nickel magnetic pads self-align dies for fine-pitch hybrid bonding
idea: Pattern soft-magnetic FeNi pads at die corners and matching hard-magnetic pads on the target wafer; dies placed by a coarse pick-and-place onto a thin water film self-register to <200 nm via magnetic plus capillary forces before Cu/SiCN hybrid bonding.
why: Die-to-wafer bonding throughput and aligner capital choke HBM stacking (fact 6); magnetic self-assembly could run ~10x faster on cheaper tools, enabling known-good-die stacks with fewer TSV-heavy wafer stacks.

title: Copper bond per bitline gives every bitline its own sense amp
idea: Hybrid-bond the cell-array wafer face-to-face to a logic wafer at ~0.4 um Cu pitch so every short local bitline (64 cells) lands on its own sense amplifier built in an advanced logic node, abolishing open/folded bitline sharing.
why: Moves the 49% periphery (fact 7) to dense logic, cuts Cb ~4x so Cs can drop toward 1-2 fF (fact 1), and per-bitline sensing enables column-granular activation that ends 128x overfetch (fact 8).

title: Zinc-tin oxide channels give indium-free 64-tier BEOL DRAM
idea: Use ALD amorphous Zn-Sn-O at ~250 C as the lateral access-transistor channel of each BEOL tier, stacked 64 high over CMOS; Sn 5s orbitals carry mobility in place of In while keeping wide-gap off-current near 1e-19 A/um.
why: Keeps the oxide-semiconductor leakage advantage (fact 3) and BEOL stackability (fact 2) while removing indium supply risk, so high-tier oxide 3D DRAM can reach commodity volume.

title: Strontium-calcium titanate superlattice gives k near 200 inside tiers
idea: Grow ALD SrTiO3/CaTiO3 nanolaminates with 1-2 nm periods whose interfacial strain stabilizes a high-k paraelectric state at ~8 nm thickness (k ~150-250) on TiN, crystallized by millisecond flash anneal; a lateral cylinder ~150 nm long inside a 40 nm tier then stores ~5 fF.
why: Meets the charge wall (fact 1) with a short lateral capacitor that fits one tier, making lateral 3D cells viable (fact 2) without Ru electrodes; Ca is abundant and Sr moderately available.

title: Zirconia antiferroelectric capacitors double stored charge per lateral cavity
idea: Tune ~7 nm ALD ZrO2 (thickness plus Si/Al doping) into an antiferroelectric pinched-loop state whose field-induced polar transition sits just under the 1 V storage voltage, so the capacitor releases ~2x the charge of a linear dielectric of equal area; with no remanent polarization it avoids ferroelectric fatigue.
why: Doubles effective charge per area (fact 1), letting lateral 3D capacitors be half as long and tiers thinner (fact 2), using Zr, O and Al rather than Hf or Ru.

title: Tin monoxide p-type transistors put sense amps above the array
idea: Pair p-type SnO (Sn2+, sputter/ALD at ~250 C) with n-type ZTO to build complementary oxide sense amplifiers, sub-wordline drivers and local decoders in a BEOL tier directly over each 3D-DRAM mat, so periphery tiles the mat footprint rather than flanking it.
why: Periphery is ~49% of the die (fact 7); stacking local periphery over the mat with low-temperature CMOS gives ~30-40% die shrink with no second wafer or hybrid bond, and no indium.

title: Hydrogen anneal reshapes hole arrays into stacked silicon-on-nothing tiers
idea: Etch rows of deep holes with periodically modulated diameter by cycled DRIE, then anneal at ~1100 C in H2 in a hydrogen-capable university furnace: Si surface migration closes each row into a stack of flat buried voids, leaving thin single-crystal Si membranes between them as device tiers and the voids as capacitor or isolation cavities.
why: Multiple crystalline lateral-transistor tiers from a bulk wafer using only i-line litho, DRIE and a furnace (fact 2), no epi reactor or bonder; an ideal 4-8-tier lateral-cell testbed.

title: Carbon-chain block copolymers self-assemble the 4F2 cell grid without EUV
idea: Spin cylinder-forming PS-b-PMMA (or high-chi PS-b-PDMS) on a coarse e-beam/i-line guide pattern so it self-assembles a hexagonal hole array at 20-24 nm pitch, remove the minority cores, and transfer the holes into an Al2O3 hard mask for vertical-channel 4F2 pillars.
why: Replaces 2-3 EUV layers (fact 4) with a polymer coat and hotplate while reaching 4F2 density (1.5x vs 6F2); needs only a spinner, oven and RIE found in any university fab.

title: Nitrogen-rich strained SiN bilayers roll planar arrays into memory scrolls
idea: Build a planar oxide-TFT DRAM array with i-line litho on a stress-graded SiNx bilayer over a sacrificial layer; releasing it makes the membrane self-roll into a 10-20-winding Swiss roll, turning the 2D array into a 3D cylinder with ~15 effective tiers per footprint, wired out through the unrolled tail.
why: Gets 3D layer count from 2D lithography with zero high-aspect etching (facts 2, 4); rolled-up nanomembranes are an established university technique, so a prototype memory scroll is buildable now.

title: Oxygen pinch-off of Bosch scallops yields stacked nanowire tiers
idea: Etch tall Si fins with a deliberately scalloped Bosch (SF6/C4F8) cycle, then dry-oxidize at ~1000 C so the narrow necks between scallops oxidize through first, leaving vertically stacked, oxide-isolated horizontal Si nanowires, one per scallop, as lateral access-transistor tiers.
why: Crystalline stacked lateral channels (fact 2) from bulk Si using only DRIE and a furnace; scallop period sets tier pitch (~100-200 nm) for 4-10-tier university demonstrations.

title: Fluorine vapor XeF2 carves lateral capacitor cavities in poly-Si stacks
idea: Deposit an LPCVD poly-Si/SiO2 multilayer, etch a vertical slit, and expose it to XeF2 vapor, which isotropically recesses only the poly-Si (>1000:1 to SiO2) by a timed 100-200 nm; ALD then lines the horizontal cavities with TiN/ZrO2/TiN as lateral capacitors for 8-16 tiers.
why: Demonstrates lateral 3D-DRAM capacitor formation (fact 2) with a plasma-free, stiction-free etch present in most university MEMS labs, avoiding SiGe epi entirely.

title: Sodium-calcium glass panels host display-style oxide DRAM tiers
idea: Fabricate stacked oxide-TFT 2T0C/1T1C arrays on SiN-barriered soda-lime (Na, Ca, Si, O) glass using i-line or proximity litho and sputtering, as the university prototype of a display-fab memory line where one Gen-8.5 panel (~5.5 m2) offers ~78x the area of a 300 mm wafer.
why: Attacks capital intensity (fact 4) by repurposing idle LCD fabs and cheap glass for bulk-capacity, refresh-light memory tiers built from the most abundant elements on the table.

title: Magnesiothermic reduction turns oxide pillars into porous-silicon capacitor electrodes
idea: Pattern SiO2 storage-node pillars by e-beam or i-line litho, react them with Mg vapor at ~650 C (2Mg + SiO2 -> Si + 2MgO), strip MgO in dilute HCl, and keep the resulting doped mesoporous Si as an electrode with ~5-10x surface area, finished with ALD Al2O3/ZrO2 and TiN.
why: Multiplies capacitance per footprint at low aspect ratio (fact 1), so a 10:1 pillar could hold what a 60:1 pillar holds; needs only a furnace, wet bench and ALD.

title: Aluminum anodization pores template litho-free vertical 4F2 cells
idea: Anodize a 300 nm sputtered Al film on Si in oxalic acid (two-step, seeded by a sparse e-beam pre-pattern for long-range order) to form a hexagonal pore array at 40-60 nm pitch, then ALD a ZTO shell channel, Al2O3 dielectric and TiN core gate down each pore with the capacitor on top.
why: Defines a 4F2 vertical array by electrochemistry and ALD alone, with no EUV (fact 4) and minimal masks; a beaker, power supply and ALD tool suffice.

title: Aluminum layer exchange crystallizes each tier's silicon below 450 C
idea: For each stacked tier, sputter Al, let a thin oxide membrane form, sputter a-Si on top and anneal at ~425 C so Si diffuses through the Al and crystallizes beneath it as large-grain (>10 um) (111)-textured poly-Si; etch away the displaced Al, counter-dope the Al background and build lateral transistors in the grains.
why: Near-crystalline lateral channels for every 3D tier (fact 2) inside BEOL thermal budget over finished periphery, using only sputter, furnace and wet etch.

title: Silicon-oxygen HSQ resist becomes the patterned inter-tier dielectric directly
idea: Spin hydrogen silsesquioxane, write cell-isolation and inter-tier oxide patterns by e-beam, develop, and cure it into a SiO2-like dielectric that stays in the device, so each tier's isolation is written rather than deposited, masked and etched; repeat per tier on alignment marks.
why: Drops deposition, hardmask and etch steps per tier (fact 4), avoids plasma damage to channels (fact 3), and lets a university e-beam tool prototype multi-tier arrays at ~10 nm features.

title: Siloxane soft-stamp nanoimprint copies one e-beam master to every tier
idea: Write a single 4F2-pitch Si master by e-beam, cast hard-PDMS/PDMS stamps from it, and UV-nanoimprint the critical cell layer of every tier on every wafer at ~15 nm resolution, using the master only to replicate stamps and a mask aligner for overlay.
why: Capital per critical layer falls ~100x vs EUV (fact 4); imprint has been trialed by NAND makers and imprint tools are common in university fabs.

title: Phosphorus monolayer doping uniformly dopes vertical pillar sidewalls without implant
idea: Graft a self-limiting monolayer of a phosphorus-bearing molecule (e.g., diethyl vinylphosphonate) onto HF-cleaned vertical Si pillars, cap with evaporated SiO2 and spike-anneal to drive a conformal ~1e20 cm^-3, few-nm-deep n+ layer into every sidewall and pillar top.
why: Forms source/drain and buried-bitline junctions on 4F2 pillars with atomic depth control, avoiding implant shadowing at high aspect ratio (fact 4) and narrowing junction-leakage spread (fact 3); needs a wet bench and RTA.

title: Sulfur-anchored monolayers enable mask-free self-aligned contacts in stacked tiers
idea: Dip the wafer in an alkanethiol solution so a self-assembled monolayer binds only to exposed Cu lines, then ALD Al2O3 grows only on the dielectric (area-selective deposition); strip the SAM to leave metal exposed and perfectly self-aligned for the next tier's vias.
why: Each self-aligned level removes a critical alignment mask and its overlay budget (fact 4) and allows tighter via pitch in 3D stacks; a thiol bath and ALD are standard university equipment.

title: Argon-activated room-temperature bonding stacks finished oxide-TFT memory tiers
idea: Fabricate oxide-semiconductor memory tiers on separate 100 mm wafers, activate both bonding faces with an Ar fast-atom beam or Ar plasma, bond in vacuum at room temperature, then grind/etch away the donor substrate; repeat for 4-8 tiers on IR-aligned keys.
why: Stacks fully processed tiers with zero thermal budget so each is optimized independently (fact 2) and tests a known-good-tier yield model; argon is abundant (0.93% of air) and SAB bonders exist in many universities.

title: Potassium hydroxide on (110) silicon etches crystal-perfect vertical cell walls
idea: Align lines along <112> on (110) Si and etch in KOH so the slow {111} planes form atomically smooth vertical walls 20-40 nm thick at >100:1 aspect ratio; a deposited oxide/TiN wordline stack crossing the walls turns each wall into a vertical string of DRAM cells.
why: Single-crystal vertical semiconductor sheets for stacked cells (fact 2) without DRIE or EUV (fact 4), from a heated beaker; smooth walls trim the interface-trap leakage tail (fact 3).

title: Titanium angle-evaporation forms self-aligned half-gates on pillar arrays
idea: Tilt the wafer 60-75 degrees in an e-beam evaporator so Ti lands only on one face and a set height band of each pillar (neighbors shadow the rest), then nitride it; rotating between evaporations writes wordlines and contacts at self-aligned heights with no lithography.
why: Shadow-defined wordlines on 4F2 pillars remove critical masks (fact 4) and set gate length by geometry, and the gate-free face lowers GIDL (fact 3); a tilt-stage evaporator is ubiquitous in university fabs.

title: Iron-catalyzed carbon nanotube bundles form vertical through-tier bitlines
idea: Evaporate ~1 nm Fe catalyst on Al2O3 at the bottom of vertical holes through a tier stack and grow dense multi-walled CNT bundles by thermal CVD at 550-650 C, filling each hole with an electromigration-immune vertical bitline or plate line contacted by every tier.
why: Replaces tungsten fill in deep holes (resource chokepoint) where CVD metal voids at high aspect ratio (fact 2); Fe and C are abundant and CNT CVD furnaces are common in university labs.

title: Copper electroless bottom-up fill wires lateral wordline cavities
idea: After removing sacrificial SiN tiers through slits, line cavities with 2 nm ALD TiN, seed them with an aminosilane-anchored Cu nanoparticle catalyst, and fill by electroless Cu with a suppressor additive at the slit mouth so growth proceeds bottom-up and void-free.
why: Eliminates WF6 CVD and tungsten (China ~80%) from 3D wordlines and lowers wordline resistance ~3x, allowing longer wordlines with fewer driver and staircase regions (fact 7); runs on a wet bench.

title: Copper spiral coils link stacked dies wirelessly instead of TSVs
idea: Pattern 20-40 um Cu inductor coils by lift-off or plating on each thinned memory die and stack the dies with adhesive; inductive coupling carries Gb/s data per coil pair through 4-8 dies, while power arrives through a few coarse TSVs or edge wires.
why: Cuts the HBM TSV tax (fact 6): less keep-out area and TSV yield loss, and adhesive stacking replaces fine-pitch bonding; coils are single-mask university builds.

title: Zinc-oxide sacrificial release lets PDMS stamps transfer-print memory tiers
idea: Build thin-film memory tiles (oxide TFTs plus capacitors) on a ZnO sacrificial layer, undercut it in dilute acetic acid while tethers hold the tiles, pick them up with a PDMS stamp and print them onto logic or the previous tier, stacking only known-good tiles.
why: Known-good-tile stacking breaks the yield multiplication across tiers (fact 2) without wafer-scale bonders; micro-transfer printing needs only a stamp stage that universities have or can build.

title: Silver-catalyzed chemical etch drills 200:1 vertical silicon pillars
idea: Pattern a perforated Ag film by e-beam lift-off, immerse in HF/H2O2 so the Ag sinks into the Si, and carve smooth vertical pillars or holes at aspect ratios >200:1 with no plasma, used as vertical channels and deep capacitor electrodes.
why: Breaks the capacitor aspect-ratio wall (fact 1 needs AR ~115) with a beaker-cost wet etch and no plasma damage to worsen the leakage tail (fact 3); Ag use is nanograms per wafer.

title: Tin-copper solid-liquid interdiffusion bonds stack tiers without remelting earlier joints
idea: Bond each memory tier with thin Sn on Cu pads at ~250 C; the Sn fully converts to Cu3Sn/Cu6Sn5 intermetallic that melts above ~600 C, so later bonding steps never reflow earlier joints, allowing sequential 8-16-high stacks on a simple flip-chip bonder.
why: A low-cost, particle-tolerant alternative to hybrid bonding for stacked memory (fact 6) using abundant Sn and Cu, buildable in university packaging labs.

title: Bismuth-tin capillary injection fills through-tier vias at 150 C
idea: As the final back-end step, evacuate the wafer, flood it with molten Bi58Sn42 (melts at 139 C) and apply gas pressure so liquid metal is forced into 50:1 through-tier vias and staircase contacts in seconds; wipe and polish the excess for void-free vertical connections.
why: Removes tungsten and slow CVD fills from deep contacts (resource and capital) at a temperature compatible with oxide-TFT tiers; a vacuum chamber and hotplate suffice in a university lab.
